_comment: Every `expectedMs` below was worked out by hand and the arithmetic is written
out in the case's `why`. These values are NOT generated from the implementation.
If a change makes a case fail, the change is wrong until proven otherwise:
recompute the arithmetic in `why` before touching the number.
Calendar-relevant facts used, all verifiable against the IANA database:
Europe/Berlin enters CEST on 2026-03-29 at 02:00 local (that day is 23h long).
Europe/Berlin leaves CEST on 2026-10-25 at 03:00 local (that day is 25h long).

businessMsCases.name: overnight gap contributes nothing
businessMsCases.why: Monday 09:00-17:00 = 8h. Tuesday 00:00-09:00 is outside the window.

businessMsCases.name: interval entirely outside working hours
businessMsCases.why: 2026-03-07 is a Saturday; the calendar has no Saturday window.

businessMsCases.name: four whole weeks
businessMsCases.why: 28 days from a Monday = 4 weeks = 20 working days * 8h = 160h.

businessMsCases.name: DST spring forward: a 24/7 local day is 23 hours
businessMsCases.why: Local 2026-03-29 00:00 to 2026-03-30 00:00 in Berlin. Clocks jump 02:00->03:00, so the local day is 23h. This is the physically correct answer and the one a naive fixed-offset implementation gets wrong.

businessMsCases.name: DST fall back: a 24/7 local day is 25 hours
businessMsCases.why: Local 2026-10-25 00:00 to 2026-10-26 00:00 in Berlin. Clocks repeat 02:00-03:00, so the local day is 25h.

businessMsCases.name: business hours are unchanged by a DST transition
businessMsCases.why: Friday 2026-03-27 09:00-17:00 local (CET, 08:00-16:00 UTC) = 8h; weekend = 0; Monday 2026-03-30 09:00-17:00 local (CEST, 07:00-15:00 UTC) = 8h. 09:00-17:00 is eight hours on both sides of the transition.

businessMsCases.name: holidays are skipped
businessMsCases.why: Thu 2026-04-02 = 8h; Fri 04-03 Karfreitag = 0; Sat/Sun = 0; Mon 04-06 Ostermontag = 0; Tue 04-07 09:00-17:00 = 8h. Total 16h.

addBusinessMsCases.name: eight working hours from Friday afternoon land on Monday
addBusinessMsCases.why: 1h remains on Friday; the other 7h are consumed Monday 09:00-16:00.

addBusinessMsCases.name: starting outside working hours jumps to the next window
addBusinessMsCases.why: Saturday noon has no working time; the first available hour is Monday 09:00-10:00.

addBusinessMsCases.name: adding zero returns the same instant
addBusinessMsCases.why: No working time requested, so the instant is unchanged even outside a window.

addBusinessMsCases.name: a target that crosses a holiday weekend
addBusinessMsCases.why: Start is Thu 2026-04-02 15:00 local (CEST, +02). 2h remain that day (15:00-17:00). Fri 04-03 Karfreitag, Sat, Sun and Mon 04-06 Ostermontag contribute nothing. The last hour is consumed Tue 04-07 09:00-10:00 local = 08:00 UTC.
